name: Firefly Blue Ghost Mission 1
short_status: Success: landed upright in Mare Crisium Mar 2, 2025; 14 days of surface ops with 10 NASA payloads; mission concluded Mar 16, 2025.
tagline: Firefly Aerospace · United States · Lander · 2025 · Commercial and multipolar Success
stats: surface operations, plus 5 hours into the lunar night
data downlinked (51 GB of it science)

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 15 January 2025, 1:11 a.m. EST, Falcon 9 from KSC LC-39A

facts.label: Transit
facts.value: 45 days, more than 2.8 million miles traveled

facts.label: Landing
facts.value: 2 March 2025, 3:34 a.m. EST (08:34 UTC), Mare Crisium

facts.label: Landing accuracy
facts.value: Upright, within its 100-meter target next to Mons Latreille

facts.label: Payloads
facts.value: 10 NASA science and technology payloads, all operated

facts.label: Surface operations
facts.value: 346 hours of daylight plus just over 5 hours into lunar night; longest commercial lunar surface operations to date

facts.label: Data returned
facts.value: 119 GB downlinked, including 51 GB of science and technology data

facts.label: LuGRE first
facts.value: First GNSS signal acquisition and tracking en route to and on the Moon; record distance 246,000 miles

facts.label: LISTER first
facts.value: Drilled up to 3 feet; deepest robotic planetary subsurface thermal probe

facts.label: Eclipse and sunset imagery
facts.value: Total solar eclipse imaged from the surface 14 March 2025; lunar sunset 16 March 2025

facts.label: Blue Ghost Mission 2
facts.value: Targeted no earlier than 2027 (as of October 2026): far-side landing near Nassau crater with LuSEE-Night, Rashid 2 and SPIDER; Elytra Dark orbital relay with ESA Lunar Pathfinder

timeline: NASA awards Firefly a $93.3M CLPS task order for the Mare Crisium delivery
Launch at 1:11 a.m. EST on Falcon 9 from KSC LC-39A, sharing the ride with ispace RESILIENCE
Touchdown at 3:34 a.m. EST in Mare Crisium: first fully successful commercial Moon landing
LROC publishes orbital images pinpointing the lander at 18.5623 N, 61.8103 E
Images a total solar eclipse from the lunar surface as Earth blocks the Sun
Captures the lunar sunset, operates just over 5 hours into lunar night, and concludes the mission
Blue Ghost Mission 2 targeted to the lunar far side (as of Oct 2026)
